title: Office & Accounts Administrator
description:
Office & Accounts Administrator - 32,000 - 36,000 DOE - Camden
Our client, a family-owned property investment business: four companies, around 90 properties across London, Liverpool and the rest of the UK. The administrator will keep the office, the paperwork and the money flowing smoothly.
Responsibilities:
Accounts Admin
- Collect supplier invoices and utility bills as they arrive by email and post. Download bills from supplier portals.
- Check each invoice against the order, contract or agreement. Send queries to whoever placed the order.
- Rename and file every invoice using the company's expense codes, by company and property.
- Prepare the weekly payment run for approval. Approved payments are made by James or Kate; the administrator does not authorise payments.
- Load payroll and PAYE payments from the figures the bookkeeper provides.
- Send the week's invoices to the bookkeeper on a set day and keep the reference copy filed.
- Keep the bank account and supplier details list up to date and confirm any change of supplier bank details by phone before it is used.
- Act as the bookkeeper's day-to-day contact for missing invoices, receipts and queries.
- Help set up and apply the new cost codes, so every cost is allocated to a property and a company.
- Gather the information needed for VAT returns, year-end accounts and confirmation statements, to the deadlines in the calendar.

Combined Calendar
Set up and run one calendar for the whole business, with reminders far enough ahead to act on:
- Accounts: VAT returns, annual accounts, confirmation statements and payroll dates, each with a preparation window before it.
- Property: rent due dates, rent reviews, lease breaks and expiries, and tenancy renewals.
- Compliance: gas safety, electrical, fire risk, EPC and other certificates, licences and inspections.
- Insurance: renewal dates.
- People: HR dates such as probation reviews and annual reviews.

Insurance Admin
- Keep the insurance schedule up to date: policies, renewal dates, premiums and documents.
- Be the brokers' day-to-day contact for documents, changes and renewals.
- Tell the brokers in writing about changes such as vacant units, changes of use and building works, as directed.
- Keep the claims file in order.
- Review policy documents and make sure their terms and conditions are kept to, for example inspections of vacant units, heating and water rules, tenant referencing and electrical safety reports. Diarise each condition and flag anything not being met.

Office, Post and Records
- Clear the backlog of paper records in the office: sort, scan where useful, file, and send to storage.
- Set up and keep a retention and destruction schedule for stored records, on the accountant's advice.
- Keep the office running: supplies, equipment, deliveries and visitors.
- Help with the office move in May 2027.

Company and Legal Administration
- Keep company records up to date for the four companies and prepare Companies House filings for approval.
- Keep registers of leases, tenancies, licences and key documents, and know where the originals are.

HR Admin
- Keep staff files: contracts, right-to-work checks, holiday and absence records.
- Diarise probation and annual reviews, and help prepare them.
- Help with recruitment admin: adverts, CVs, interview scheduling and onboarding.
- Keep HR policies filed and up to date, with the HR adviser.

IT & Systems
- Be the day-to-day contact for the IT provider: new users, laptops, access and faults.
- Help move files into the new shared document system and keep its folders tidy.

Supporting the team
- Support Associate Director with diary management, meeting notes, trackers and document preparation.
- Support the Property Manager, with document chasing, filing and tenancy paperwork. Keep the property management software, Konnexions, fully up to date and well managed: tenants, leases, rents, deposits, certificates, contacts and documents. The team needs all the information there to be accurate and current, because they rely on it to manage the portfolio.
- Work with the Liverpool team on shared admin tasks.

Skills and Experience Required:
- Minimum 5 years' experience in office or accounts administration within property
- Be confident with Xero and Excel
- Experience with property management software
- Excellent accuracy and attention to detail
- AAT Level 2 or equivalent bookkeeping knowledge

Salary: 32,000 - 36,000 DOE
Working Hours: Monday - Friday, 9am - 5:30pm, office based

title: Community Data Administrator
description:
About us

We are a leading integrated media and marketing services company at the heart of a community of over 590,000 UK healthcare professionals. With more than 30 years of experience, we produce industry-leading content and experiences through our award-winning brands, publications, and events. We produce trusted, data-driven content that informs and inspires healthcare professionals across the UK and Europe. We are a Great Place to Work and UK's Best Workplaces for Women certified employer, offering a range of benefits including 28 days annual leave (rising to 30 days after 2 years) excluding bank holidays, private healthcare insurance, flexible working and more.

The Role

Our Community Data Administrator will be responsible for the quality, coverage, depth and development of the organisation's HCP community. The role will ensure we have a high-quality, accurate, comprehensive, current, relevant and growing audience that meets the needs of the business and our clients.

They will develop a detailed understanding of the organisation's HCP data and the wider addressable HCP market, identifying where we have strong coverage, where gaps exist and what actions we can take to address them. They will use first- and third-party data, market intelligence and behavioural and engagement data to understand the composition and health of our community and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.

This is a highly analytical role for someone who loves working with data, numbers and solving problems. They will interrogate datasets, spot patterns and anomalies, assess data quality and freshness, identify gaps and translate findings into clear actions.

Working closely with teams across the organisation, they will help source and evaluate new data, improve HCP profiling and segmentation, strengthen our understanding of audience engagement and ensure our HCP community becomes increasingly accurate, complete, current and commercially valuable.

Location: Central London (Hybrid)

Reporting to: Digital Director

Expected start date: January 2027

Salary: £30,000 to £38,000 per annum, depending on experience

Key Responsibilities:

Data Quality & Governance

Take ownership of the overall health of the organisation's HCP database, including accuracy, completeness, recency, duplication, consistency, consent and compliance. Establish clear definitions and standards for data quality and regularly measure the database against them, including agreed definitions for active HCPs, inactive HCPs, dormant records, complete profiles and verified HCPs. Identify data quality issues and work with relevant teams to implement solutions and continually improve the reliability of our data.

HCP Coverage & Gap Analysis

Build a detailed understanding of the organisation's coverage of the HCP market and identify gaps by profession, specialty, geography, seniority and other relevant characteristics. Develop clear, data-led plans to address priority audience gaps and measure the impact of actions taken.

Data Enrichment

Identify opportunities to enhance existing HCP records with additional data points and attributes, improving the completeness and depth of our profiles. Determine which additional attributes would provide the greatest audience, editorial and commercial value and identify appropriate sources for obtaining them.

Data Freshness & Engagement

Assess how recently and frequently HCPs interact with the organisation across our brands, websites, newsletters, events, CPD platforms, surveys and other products. Develop and maintain an HCP engagement scoring methodology that combines behavioural signals across the business to provide a consistent view of audience engagement. Use engagement and recency data to understand the active audience within our overall community and identify opportunities to increase engagement.

Audience Re-engagement & Cleansing

Identify inactive, ageing, duplicate, incomplete or low-confidence records. Work with relevant teams to determine appropriate approaches for re-engagement, verification, consolidation, suppression or removal. Monitor the effectiveness of re-engagement and cleansing activity and use the findings to continually improve our approach.

Data Matching & Deduplication

Develop approaches for identifying duplicate HCP records and matching individuals across different the organisation datasets, platforms and data sources. Investigate conflicting information and establish appropriate rules for determining the most reliable and current information. Support the development of an increasingly consistent and accurate single view of each HCP across the organisation.

Segmentation & Audience Insight

Develop meaningful HCP segments based on profession, specialty, geography, seniority, demographics, behaviour, engagement, recency and other relevant characteristics. Analyse these segments to identify patterns, opportunities and changes in audience behaviour. Translate complex data into clear insights that can be understood and acted upon by teams across the business.

Data Acquisition & Gap Closure

Research and evaluate new first- and third-party data sources that could strengthen the organisation's HCP community. Assess potential sources based on quality, coverage, accuracy, recency, compliance, cost and likely incremental value. Develop data-led recommendations for acquiring or generating data to address identified audience gaps and measure whether those interventions successfully improve coverage.

Commercial Audience Analysis

Work closely with Sales and other commercial teams to understand current and emerging client audience requirements. Translate these requirements into data needs and assess the organisation's ability to reach relevant HCP audiences. Identify areas where strengthening our data could create new commercial opportunities or improve our existing audience proposition.

Measurement & Reporting

Develop and maintain reporting on the health and development of the organisation's HCP community. Monitor key metrics including database size, net growth, coverage, completeness, duplication, freshness, active and inactive audiences, engagement and enrichment. Move beyond simply reporting numbers by identifying what the data tells us, highlighting emerging issues and opportunities and making clear recommendations for action.

HCP Data Expertise

Become the organisation's internal authority on our HCP community. Develop a comprehensive understanding of what data we hold, where it comes from, how reliable and current it is, how our audiences engage with the organisation, where gaps exist and what opportunities there are to improve the data. Support teams across the business with questions about HCP audience size, composition, coverage and engagement.

About You

We're looking for someone who is naturally curious and genuinely enjoys working with data. You'll have a highly analytical mind, an exceptional eye for detail and a tendency to ask "why?" and "what does this tell us?" rather than simply accepting numbers at face value.

You'll enjoy getting into the detail of datasets, spotting patterns, gaps and inconsistencies and working out how to solve them. You'll be organised, methodical and comfortable working with large volumes of data, while also being able to step back and understand the bigger picture.

Most importantly, you'll be someone who lives and breathes data - excited by numbers, curious about what they can tell us and always looking for ways to make the organisation's HCP community better, more current and more valuable.

title: Trainee HR Administrator
description:
Thinking About a Career Change? Why Not Choose HR?

If you've reached a crossroads in your professional life and are looking for a fresh start in a people-focused, rewarding industry then Human Resources might be exactly what you're looking for.

Many of our candidates come from diverse professional backgrounds retail, customer service, administration, healthcare, education, hospitality, and more. What they all have in common is the desire to do meaningful work, support others, and build a stable, long-term career.

Our HR Career Change Programme

Whether you're working full-time, part-time, or in between roles, our online learning and personalised recruitment support can help you make a successful move into the HR profession often in just a few months.

Please note that this is a training course and fees apply.

Why Human Resources?

The HR profession is growing steadily across all sectors. As businesses put more focus on employee wellbeing, development, and company culture, skilled HR professionals are more important than ever.

Even entry-level roles in HR offer strong salaries, clear progression routes, and opportunities to specialise over time (in areas like learning & development, recruitment, employee relations, and more).

- HR Administrator - £27,000+
- HR Assistant - £30,000+
- HR Officer - £35,000+
- HR Advisor - £38,500+
- HR Manager - £55,000+

And with hybrid and remote roles increasingly common in HR, the flexibility is there too.

The CIPD Level 3 Certificate in People Practice is the industry-standard entry point into Human Resources. It's assignment-based (no exams), and is delivered fully online with expert tutor support.
- Accredited by the Chartered Institute of Personnel & Development (CIPD)

We've been helping career changers break into new roles since 2007-and our 4.8 Trustpilot rating shows how serious we are about your success.

You'll get:
- A professionally written, HR-focused CV
- Job-matching advice tailored to your experience and location
- Application support, interview prep, and mock interviews
- Ongoing 1-to-1 guidance to help you land your first HR role

Step 3 - Start Your New HR Career

Most of our candidates secure their first HR job within 3-6 months of qualifying-and often sooner if they're based near a major town or city.

And to give you confidence, we offer a Money Back Guarantee:
If we can't help you secure a role within 12 months of passing your qualification, we'll refund your training fees.

Flexible, Affordable, Achievable

To make things easier, we offer flexible payment options to spread the cost of your training over 12 months-so you can get qualified without financial pressure.

Most of our candidates secure their first HR job within 3-6 months of qualifying-and often sooner if they're based near a major town or city.

If we can't help you secure a role within 12 months of passing your qualification, we'll refund your training fees.

Flexible, Affordable, Achievable

To make things easier, we offer flexible payment options to spread the cost of your training over 12 months-so you can get qualified without financial pressure.

Moores of London creates bespoke corporate gifts, branded merchandise, and premium hospitality products. Working directly with the Managing Director, the Operations and Client Support Coordinator takes confirmed client orders from initial handover right through to delivery and invoicing. This is a dynamic, hands-on role combining client administration with physical stock handling, packing, and dispatch.

Key Projects & Systems Development

In addition to daily operations, the successful candidate will work with the Managing Director to streamline and modernize operational systems:
- Data Cleanup: Audit existing client, supplier, order, stock, and sample databases. Consolidate scattered files, eliminate duplicate records, verify missing details, and establish standard data naming conventions.
- Process & Tool Setup: Document existing order and invoicing workflows. Assist in building and maintaining the company s first live order tracker, and help evaluate and implement dedicated invoicing software and a CRM as the business scales.

Essential Criteria
- Relevant Experience: Background in order administration, client service, inventory management, or order fulfilment, with proven confidence tracking multiple deadlines.
- Communication & Precision: Professional phone manner, excellent written communication, and strong attention to detail when auditing prices, quantities, and financial documents.
- Digital Literacy: Practical working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, email workflows, and shared digital folders.
- Hands-on Mindset: Willingness and capability to regularly undertake physical warehouse/fulfilment duties (packing, lifting, and organizing stock/cartons).

Desirable Criteria
- Demonstrated experience developing or refining administrative processes (e.g., invoicing procedures, stocktaking frameworks, order processing workflows).
- Familiarity with using AI tools to automate routine administrative tasks.

We're working with a well-established international drinks business to recruit a Supply Chain Co-ordinator to join their team in London.

You'll be working closely with teams across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Procurement and Logistics, helping to make sure forecasts, stock levels and supply plans are all working together.

description:

You will be working as part of an established team, helping to manage and coordinate our temporary workforce and ensuring our Blue Chip clients receive an excellent level of service. Strong Excel and Microsoft Office skills are important, as is the ability to juggle several priorities at once, We need someone with energy, initiative and a strong work ethic who is not afraid to get involved, support the wider team and learn new things. If you have previously worked in sales administration or recruitment, even better - you already understand the importance of great customer service, strong relationships and making things happen.

- Managing and coordinating temporary workers to ensure client shifts are covered and run smoothly

title: Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator
description:
Single Homeless Project has an opportunity for a Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator to join our experienced and committed teams based in Islington . You will join us on a full-time, permanent basis. In return, you will receive a competitive salary starting at £29,822.41 and rising incrementally to £32,034.46 per annum.

We re London s leading homelessness charity and we get things done.

In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we re not shying away. We re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up.

We re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own.

Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable.

We re not perfect, but we re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn t just a job. It s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind.

About the Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator role:

Recovery looks different for everyone, and meaningful opportunities can be a powerful part of helping people move forward. As a Recovery and Opportunities Coordinator, you ll take the lead in creating a programme that gives clients across Ashley Road, Milton House and Highbury New Park the chance to build confidence, strengthen their wellbeing, discover new interests, develop new skills and take positive steps towards greater independence.

This is a hands on and creative role where you ll turn ideas into activities that people genuinely want to take part in. You ll design and deliver engaging group work covering areas such as mental and physical health, relationships, substance use, life skills and learning, while creating opportunities that support clients to prepare for moving on to more independent accommodation. You ll use a strengths based and trauma-informed approach, adapting what you offer to respond to people s interests, goals and experiences.

You ll also look beyond our services to create more opportunities for clients. Building strong relationships with community organisations, statutory services, specialist agencies and lived experience networks, you ll help connect people with the resources, activities and support available around them. Alongside this, you ll champion co-production, support colleagues, volunteers and peers to get involved in delivering the programme, and help make recovery and social inclusion a visible part of everyday service delivery.

About you:
- You have experience developing, coordinating and facilitating groups and activities, with a good understanding of group dynamics and how to support others to deliver them confidently and effectively.
- You re creative, enthusiastic and proactive, with the confidence to turn ideas into meaningful opportunities and encourage clients, colleagues, volunteers and peers to get involved.
- You re confident building positive working relationships and partnerships with a range of internal and external services, helping to open up new opportunities for the people we support.
- You understand how to engage, motivate and inspire people experiencing multiple disadvantage, including the barriers that can make participation more difficult, and can create a positive and welcoming atmosphere.
- You re committed to inclusive practice, creating environments where people from different backgrounds feel respected and able to participate, while maintaining clear and appropriate professional boundaries.

Our attractive benefits package includes:
- A salary increase after successfully completing six month's probationary period
- A 37.5 hour working week including flexible working hours (core hours are 10am 4pm) in non-accommodation services
- 25 days annual leave, increasing annually to the maximum 30 days (plus paid Bank Holidays),
- A contributory pension scheme: Single Homeless Project will contribute the equivalent of 5% of your annual salary
- Staff Health Cash Plan and discounts scheme
- Comprehensive and integrated training programme designed specifically to develop the skills and knowledge involved in our work

Don t miss out on this great opportunity to join the Single Homeless Project team please click apply now to become our Recovery & Opportunities Coordinator ? - we'd like to hear from you!

title: Part Time Receptionist/Administrator
description: The North London Health Centre is looking to recruit an enthusiastic and reliable individual to join our Reception team. This is an in person role, 18-24 hours per week over 3 or 4 days Monday to Friday. Shifts will be 6 hours per day either starting at 8.00am or 12.30pm. Please do not apply if you wish to work remotely. The applicant will be able to work under their own initiative and be able to contribute to the overall work of the practice team. Previous experience of working in a similar role is essential . The applicant must be flexible with regards to sessions worked each week and would be required to be available between the hours of 8am-6:30pm and provide cover for holidays and any sickness cover. -To make appointments and book patients in when they arrive for an appointment and to provide a helpful and friendly service to patients. -To answer telephones promptly ensuring that all in-coming lines are covered at all times. -To ensure daily tasks are completed and managed daily. -Responding and dealing with incoming emails to the practice. -To comply with all relevant practice procedures, regulations and protocols and to maintain confidentiality at all times with particular reference to patient records. -Work efficiently with other teams within the practice -To undertake any other duties as deemed appropriate by the Practice. -Action repeat prescription requests promptly -Opening mail and ensuring that all correspondence is scanned and attached to patients computer records Reception Duties - Ensure efficiency of the surgeries by monitoring the arrival of patients and the flow of patients into consulting and treatment rooms. - Ensure that patients without appointments, but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. - Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover, ensure all procedures are completed. - Advise patients of relevant charges for private services, accept payment and issue receipts where required. -Respond to all queries and requests for assistance from patients and other visitors. -Ensure reception and waiting areas are kept neat and tidy. Management of appointment system - Ensure total familiarity with all appointment systems in effect including regular and incidental variations. - Book appointments and recalls. - Monitor effectiveness of the system and report any problems or variations required. Operation of the Telephone System Receive and make telephone calls as required.Divert and take messages as appropriate. Start and End of Day Procedures - Open up premises at the start of the day and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. - Secure premises at the end of the day, ensure the building is totally secured, internal lights off and alarm activated. General Responsibilities: -Ensure total familiarity with all computer programmes which affect your work -Ensure that your work area is kept neat and tidy. - Monitor effectiveness of the various systems you operate and report any problems or variations required. Special Requirements of the post: An understanding, acceptance and adherence to the need for strict confidentiality. An ability to use own judgement, resourcefulness, common sense and local knowledge to respond to patients enquiries and requests. Excellent communication and secretarial skills. Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate Any other delegated duties considered appropriate to the post.

title: Programme Administrator
description: This is a 12-month, fixed-term post with an immediate start, supporting the development of a new project for multiprofessional roles in primary care across Islington and London. They will work closely with the Borough Training Hub Programme Manager, Training Hub Clinical Lead, and the Workforce Development Lead to provide reliable administrative support to this project and wider programme activity. This post will suit someone with experience in an administrative or junior programme management role who wants to progress into a varied, education-focused position within a close, high-functioning programme team. They will provide senior administration and coordination as needed on this project and the wider portfolio; help organise webinars and training sessions; update website content; prepare mailouts and communications; provide secretarial support for meetings; and maintain clear action logs and records. Strong organisation and communication skills are essential, along with a good working knowledge of Outlook, Excel, and Word. The role offers the opportunity to learn about programme planning and management, as well as how to use digital platforms to deliver education and training. The successful applicant must be able to work both autonomously and as part of a team. Support the effective delivery of the multi-professional project and wider programme administration Act as a point of contact, managing the shared inboxes, dealing with enquiries and providing support Provide administrative and secretarial support for programme activities, including training sessions and meetings, by sending invites and preparing agendas, papers, and notes. Maintain programme action logs, take minutes, and track progress on actions Keep accurate records and data on training activity and placements across the boroughs, using spreadsheets and programme systems Work with the Borough Programme Manager and Clinical Lead to gather local training needs and workforce demand to inform learning offers, and support the evaluation and reporting of training impact and attendance Produce resource packs and communication content for newsletters and websites. This includes regularly updating website pages and keeping up-to-date distribution lists. Lead the administration processes for approving new educators and learning environments across the five North Central London boroughs. This includes reviewing application paperwork, answering applicant queries promptly, and arranging approval assessments Finalise approval documentation following panel feedback and liaise with national and regional education teams Set up and maintain the admission processes for multi-professional supervisor training courses across London ICS Training Hubs Manage the event calendar, promote sessions (flyers, sign-ups) Other responsibilities to include: Maintain relationships with NHS Workforce Training Education team and primary care stakeholders, including accredited clinical and educator supervisor programme and apprenticeship leads Attend relevant meetings and forums as required to support project and programme activity Support the coordination of local and West North London (WNL) ICB, and pan-London training offers for the primary care workforce The post-holder may at times be required to undertake other duties of a similar nature, as reasonably required by their line manager. There may also be occasions when the post holders role and skill set may be required to support other workforce programme activity within IGPF, so flexibility is essential. Working relationships The postholder will work closely with: Borough Training Hub Programme Manager Workforce Development Lead Islington Training Hub Clinical Lead NCL Education Faculty Programme Directors and clinical educators Education Faculty & Quality team Islington GP Federation & practices London ICS Training Hub and associated colleagues NHS England Workforce Training Education team

title: Receptionist
description: Essex Lodge Surgery is looking for 2 Part Time experienced GP receptionists Must have excellent communication and customer service skills to join our friendly team The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the reception area, including the provision of clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team. Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the reception team may include all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the practice manager/partners, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations, and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Process appointment requests for today/future appointment from patients in person Using your own judgment and communication skills, ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Deal with home visit requests Ensure 2 week wait referral are emailed as soon as you receive them, completed tracker and file Ensure 2 week wait folder if checked on a daily basis Patient notes and correspondence: Retrieve and re-file records as required, ensuring strict alphabetical order is adhered to Ensure correspondence, reports, results etc. are filed promptly and in the correct records, ensuring that all recent correspondence is available when patients are seen. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover, and ensure procedures are completed Where possible check the contact details for patients, address, contact numbers and recording next of kin details and carers Process patients requests for change of address and contact numbers Enter patient information on to the computer as required Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information Managing the surgery's generic email accounts, dealing with requests and forwarding relevant message to other members staff when required Help promote NHS Friends and Family Questionnaires and other initiatives set by CCG and NHS England. Scanning correspondence with accuracy in patients electronic medical records Filing and retrieving paperwork Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Handing completed repeat prescription to patients, checking names and addresses Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Monitoring of stationery and other clinical supplies to ensure order requests are placed to maintain adequate stock Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the partners or the practice manager. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way, free from hazards Actively reporting health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable adults and children Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner that is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, with such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Ensuring mandatory training is undertaken when required to do so. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audits where appropriate Flexibility: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive description of every duty performed by the receptionist, but rather a guide to the type and nature of the duties. In Essex Lodge Surgery, flexibility in the duties undertaken and the hours worked are essential to achieve the objectives of a smooth running practice. The post holder is required to carry out any duties that fall within the scope of this role, that may reasonably be requested by the Partners or the Practice Manager and that relate to the efficiency and smooth running of the Practice.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking to recruit an administrator to join our friendly team on a permanent contact, immediate start. The successful applicant will be required to work full time (37.5 hours), shifts between 8am and 8pm Monday and Tuesday to Friday 8am and 6.30pm. Applicants must be flexible and reliable. The purpose of the role is to: Assist with referral letters, hospital correspondence, workflow, scanning, call and recall and quarterly submission. To receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. And to provide efficient, helpful, informative and supportive reception and administration services to patients and members of the primary health care team. Undertake a variety of administrative and clinical duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice including the provision of clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the Practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Specific delegated clinical tasks under the supervision of the GP Partners in accordance to practice guidelines Join our busy, forward-thinking GP practice as an Administration & Workflow Coordinator, where youll play a vital role in keeping patient care running safely, efficiently, and seamlessly behind the scenes. This is a dynamic position at the heart of the practice, managing clinical systems such as EMIS, Abtrace and AccuRx, coordinating referrals, processing medical reports, and ensuring all patient communications and records are handled accurately and in line with NHS and practice standards. You will work closely with clinicians, hospitals, and patients to support timely care, maintain workflows, and contribute to key areas such as Quality Outcomes Framework (QOF), audits, and risk management. The role also includes reception support, handling patient queries, and ensuring a high-quality, patient-focused service at all times. We are looking for someone organised, proactive, and detail-oriented, with strong communication skills and the ability to manage competing priorities. You should be confident using clinical systems, able to problem-solve independently, and comfortable working in a fast-paced healthcare environment. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who wants to make a real impact in primary care, develop their skills, and be part of a supportive team committed to delivering high-quality patient care. Duties and Responsibilities Duties and responsibilities may vary from time to time under the direction of the Business Practice Manager and Partners, depending on practice workload, staffing levels, and evolving service needs. All tasks must be carried out in accordance with practice policies, procedures, and relevant guidelines. Manage and maintain document workflow systems, ensuring timely and accurate processing of all incoming and outgoing clinical correspondence. Process referrals in the absence of the medical secretary, ensuring compliance with practice protocols and timely submission. Manage requests for medical reports, including insurance reports and copies of medical records, ensuring appropriate authorisation and turnaround times. Advise patients on applicable fees for private (non-GMS) services, process payments, and issue receipts in line with practice policy. Liaise with hospitals and external providers to ensure patients receive appropriate appointments and follow-ups. Monitor and manage workflow systems to ensure all tasks are completed within required timeframes. Maintain up-to-date scanning and document filing processes. Support call and recall systems to ensure patients are invited for relevant reviews, screenings, and follow-ups. Process and distribute incoming and outgoing mail efficiently. Process pathology results via electronic systems in accordance with practice protocols. Manage online requests, including patient queries and emails, ensuring timely and appropriate responses. Undertake accurate data entry, coding, and summarising of patient records in line with clinical standards. Respond to enquiries from patients, colleagues, healthcare professionals, and external organisations in a professional and timely manner. Provide general administrative support including document preparation, filing, photocopying, and scanning. Support delivery of the Quality Outcomes Framework (QOF) and other contractual requirements. Assist with audits, data collection, and risk management activities. Attend non-clinical meetings as required and provide accurate minute taking. Maintain and update the practice website as required. Report building or facilities issues in the absence of management. Provide first-line support for basic IT issues and escalate where necessary. Provide reception cover as required, including processing repeat prescriptions and ensuring prescriptions are ready within 48 hours where appropriate. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries and ensure adequate stock of consumables. Deliver an efficient and patient-focused reception service. Handle general enquiries, explain procedures, and book appointments appropriately. Use judgement to prioritise and manage patients requiring urgent attention without disrupting service flow. Register new patients and temporary residents, ensuring all procedures are completed accurately. Manage telephone calls, including taking and relaying messages accurately and promptly. Record home visit requests clearly and escalate to the Duty Doctor where appropriate. Act on clinician requests for further information, ensuring all documentation and follow-up actions are completed. Support the review and updating of practice policies and procedures as required. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate. The above list of duties is not exhaustive and may be subject to change as deemed necessary.

title: Receptionist/Administrator

title: Administrator
description: We have a great opportunity to join our surgeryas an Administrator . Ideally, you will have experience of managing childhood immunisation programmes and new patient registrations, alongside general practice administration.The role is 16 hours per week over 4 days, working 4 hours per day . Working times can be arranged around school runs, making this an ideal opportunity for someone looking for part-time hours. The role includes a varied range of responsibilities, including: Childhood Immunisations: Ensure that all patients aged 5 years and under are appropriately invited for their childhood immunisations and that immunisation records and schedules are accurately maintained and kept up to date. New Patient Registrations Undertake the administrative and clerical processes associated with new patient registrations, including processing electronic and paper registration forms accurately and promptly. Liaise with colleagues and relevant external organisations as required. General Administration Provide administrative support across other areas of the practice, contributing to the effective day-to-day running of the service. The successful candidate will be organised, reliable and able to work effectively as part of a busy team, with excellent attention to detail and a commitment to delivering a high-quality service. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator . On occasion, there may be a requirement to undertake additional duties, depending on factors such as workload and staffing levels: Childhood Immunisations: Manage the administrative processes relating to childhood immunisations, ensuring invitations, records and schedules are accurate and kept up to date. New Patient Registrations: Manage the administrative processes associated with new patient registrations, ensuring registrations are processed accurately and promptly. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: Childhood immunisations and registration Registering new-born babies Arranging baby health checks appointment with a doctor and first immunisation appointment with nurse (appointments must be given at 8 weeks of age, in line with public health targets) Book all babies for their immunisations and follow up on those who DNA. Search and recalling patients for immunisations weekly-monthly. Nominated administrative person, responsible for contacting Health Visitors re patients who DNR-DNA. Explain practice arrangements and registration requirements to new patients and patients requesting temporary registration. Ensure all required registration procedures and documentation are completed accurately. Deal with telephone and other enquiries relating to patient registrations, taking messages or referring queries to the appropriate team member where necessary. Enter and update patient information on the clinical system as required. Ensure regular and temporary patients are registered on the clinical system promptly and accurately. Liaise with colleagues and relevant external organisations regarding registration queries, in accordance with practice policies and procedures. Other administration tasks To assist other administration roles covering sickness and annual leave. Assist with any other reasonable requests by the management or partners. Attend Clinical meetings and take accurate minutes. Attend Open Business meeting and take accurate minutes. Attend Nurses meeting and take accurate minutes.

Actioning clinicians paperwork throughout the day. Scanning patient correspondence, actioning tasks. Respond to general enquiries and explain Surgery procedures to enquirers. JOB PURPOSE: To provide a welcoming and efficient reception service to all visitors and telephone enquiries, ensuring that the patient appointment systems function smoothly and efficiently. title: Receptionist
description: The GP Receptionist is a key front-line role within an NHS GP practice, acting as the first point of contact for patients, carers, and visitors. The role is essential in ensuring the smooth and efficient running of the practice on a daily basis. You will provide a professional, caring, and confidential reception and administrative service, supporting both patients and the clinical team. This includes managing appointments, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, processing prescriptions, and maintaining accurate patient records using clinical systems such as EMIS Web. Working in a busy primary care environment, the role requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm and organised under pressure. You will play an important part in ensuring patients are directed to the right services and receive timely, appropriate care. Overall, the GP Receptionist role is vital in supporting high-quality patient care and contributing to the effective running of the NHS GP practice. Main duties of the job Provide a professional and welcoming reception service to patients, carers, and visitors Answer telephone calls promptly, deal with enquiries, and signpost patients appropriately Book, cancel, and manage appointments using clinical systems (e.g. EMIS) Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records, ensuring confidentiality at all times Scan, file, and process incoming/outgoing correspondence and clinical documents Support clinicians with administrative tasks, including referrals and follow-ups Deal with patient related admin duties such as emails, registrations and processing online consultations. Deal with patient queries in a calm and professional manner, including difficult or distressed individuals Ensure compliance with GDPR, NHS policies, and practice procedures Work effectively as part of a team in a busy, fast-paced primary care environment Job responsibilities Patient Services Act as the first point of contact for patients in person and by telephone Deal with patient enquiries in a polite, professional, and sensitive manner Book, cancel, and amend appointments accurately and efficiently Signpost patients to appropriate clinicians or services Assist with recall of patients needing annual or monitoring reviews Administration Duties Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records using clinical systems Process repeat prescription requests following practice protocols Scan, file, and manage incoming and outgoing correspondence Support administrative tasks including referrals and clinical document processing Processing patient registrations Team Support Work closely with GPs, nurses, and the wider practice team Assist with the organisation of clinics and daily workflows Support colleagues to ensure smooth and efficient service delivery Confidentiality & Compliance Maintain strict confidentiality in line with GDPR and NHS policies Follow all practice procedures, protocols, and safeguarding requirements Ensure a professional and safe reception environment at all times General Responsibilities Manage a busy workload in a fast-paced environment Remain calm and professional when dealing with difficult or distressed patients Work effectively as part of a team and support colleagues when required Participate in training and continuous development relevant to the role

If you are approachable, organised, and enjoy working in a busy healthcare environment, we would love to hear from you! description: This position is five day a week (Mon to Fri) on site with no remote working. The trust does not offer visa sponsorship for this post. Tyson West 1 is part of Bethlem Royal Hospital. title: GP Receptionist/Administrator
description: Oxford Drive Medical Centre is looking to recruit an enthusiastic Receptionist/Administrator to join our team for 20 hours per week over 5 days (Monday to Friday inclusive). The successful applicant will be working on a set rota however due to the nature of the position would be required to work different shifts on a flexible basis to cover holidays and sickness between the hours of 8.00am and 7.00pm. The practice currently opens from 8:00am until 7:00pm Monday to Friday. Please note the shifts will mainly be middle and late shifts (eg 11:00am - 3:00pm or 3:00pm - 7:00pm) and the occasional early shift (8:00am - 12:00 noon) if cover required. Main duties include answering the telephone, greeting patients, booking appointments and transport online, taking messages, scanning and matching incoming correspondence, sending and receiving emails, filing records manually and other administrative duties. Applicants should have excellent communication skills including a clear telephone manner and be able to work in a busy environment whilst remaining calm and approachable. Computer skills are essential including MS Office. EMIS Web experience is desirable but full training will be given to the successful applicant. Job Title: Practice Receptionist/Administrator Responsible to: Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Manager & GP Partners ________________________________________________ General Information The practice provides general medical services to approximately 6,000 patients. The practice is a training practice and has two partners, a Practice Manager, GP Registrars, a Practice Nurse, a Phlebotomist and ten receptionist/ administration staff. Job Summary The Receptionist role is to provide general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Receptionists are expected to receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Principal Duties Greet all patients on arrival. Answer the telephone dealing with or redirecting enquiries. Handle general enquiries referring where necessary including giving out test results. Make new and follow-up appointments. Accept messages for the Practice Nurse. Record repeat prescriptions that are posted. Record controlled drug prescriptions. Record requests for home visits and contact the duty doctors with late calls. Register new patients following practice policy offer registration health check. Enter information onto the computer and complete Registration Link process. Clerical Duties Open mail and scan all incoming post relating to patients. Leave private, confidential and personal mail unopened for each named person or as directed. Prepare Patient Summary Printouts for home visits if requested. Check and distribute medical records/correspondence for next surgery session if appropriate. Prepare computerised repeat prescriptions following practice protocol and set out for verification and signature of doctor. File medical records, hospital reports and letters. Shred old correspondence in line with the Practice protocol. Check and file records, received from the Primary Care Support England for new patients. Extract records of patients deleted from list and send to the Primary Care Support England. Follow practice policy for recording same. Collect daily attendance figures/referral figures and enter onto computer. Extract information from computer to assist in completion of target returns. Complete appropriate GMS3 (Temporary Services) forms and file until due for submission to the Primary Care Support England. Maintain computer database. Make appointments for hospital transport. Sort, repair and maintain medical records. Maintain supplies of stationery available in reception area. Type hospital referral letters in the absence of practice secretary. Photocopy documents as required. General Duties Each morning, open premises, check heating and ventilation and restore telephone service. Purchase stamps and post mail as necessary. Make tea/coffee for doctors and other staff and participate in loading dishwasher rota. Air and tidy waiting room and consulting rooms after each session. Check doctors names and direction lights are amended as and when required. Each evening, leave reception area tidy and ready for incoming colleagues, ensuring medical records for next session have been extracted. Leave information regarding unsolved or urgent problems. Check heating and telephone system, set burglar alarm and lock up premises. Undertake any other duties as agreed with the Practice Manager and/or Doctors. The duties and responsibilities in this job description are intended to be indicative but not exhaustive of responsibilities of the post holder. As the organisation develops the requirement of the job will develop and change and the post holder will be expected to adapt to these requirements. This job description may need to be reviewed or revised from time to time as the practice develops .

Some of your duties will include:- Booking telephone appointments with patients Managing the incoming email inbox and patient requests Responding to patient queries via the Practice website dashboard Greeting patients when they arrive in the Practice and dealing with queries Calling patients on behalf of GP's to book appointments and relay information Managing incoming mail and distributing/scanning accordingly On occasion opening and closing the Practice Working with outside agencies such as Pharmacies and Care homes for patient care Registering new patients Using Practice software such as EMIS, Docman (training provided) and Office products Groves Health is a successful and trusted provider of NHS services across England. Over the past five years, we have grown from a single practice in New Malden to a team of more than 100 people, providing high-quality care to patients and communities across our four sites in New Malden, Richmond, Wimbledon and Hinchley Wood. As Groves Health continues to grow and expand the services we provide, we are looking for an enthusiastic and reliable Receptionist & Administrator to join our team at Groves New Malden. We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people, is well organised and can manage a varied workload in a busy environment. Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare or administrative setting would be beneficial, but we are also keen to hear from candidates with transferable skills and a strong commitment to providing excellent customer service. Our Reception teams play a vital role in the day-to-day running of our practices. As one of the first points of contact for patients, you will help ensure that patients receive a friendly, professional and efficient service. This is a varied role, providing the opportunity to develop your knowledge and experience across different areas of reception and administration within a busy GP surgery. Your duties will include, but are not limited to: Booking and managing telephone appointments for patients. Managing the practice email inbox and responding to patient requests. Responding to patient queries through the practice website and online services. Welcoming patients to the practice and dealing with their queries in a professional and helpful manner. Contacting patients on behalf of GPs and other members of the clinical team to arrange appointments or relay information. Receiving, sorting, scanning and distributing incoming post and correspondence. Registering new patients and ensuring their information is accurately recorded. Liaising with external organisations, including pharmacies, care homes and other healthcare services, where appropriate to support patient care. Using practice and administrative systems, including EMIS, Docman and Microsoft Office . Full training will be provided where required. Supporting colleagues with general administrative duties and contributing to the smooth running of the practice. Assisting with the opening and closing of the practice when required. We are looking for someone who: Has excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Is friendly, approachable and professional. Has a strong commitment to providing excellent patient service. title: GP Receptionist

The Practice will support continuing education and professional development in the form of attendance at study days, courses and with in-house training, as deemed appropriate for the benefit of both the individual and the Practice. Open up surgery, switching on clinicians PCs and ensuring everything is set up for the day. Ensure building security, have thorough knowledge of doors, windows and alarms. Be able to cover all care navigator roles as required including extended hour surgeries. Have knowledge of and work in accordance with practice policies and procedures. Pulling/filing notes as necessary. Scan and photocopy as required. Ensure post and clinical forms are correctly filed and waiting for collection. description: We are looking for a professional and experienced receptionist to work in our busy GP Practice. There are always opportunities to develop the roles of our staff in line with the ever-changing work we do as an NHS health service provider. We seek a reliable individual who enjoys interacting with patients and maintains a positive attitude in a fast-paced environment. General responsibilities are: Greet and direct patients and visitors. Accurately answer telephones, screen calls, and direct calls to appropriate individuals.. Answer questions and assist patients in completing registration, appointment request when it is presented via online , face to face or via telephone. Good working in teams Good communicator Our Reception team are the face of the Practice, and often the first point of contact for our patients, therefore, it is essential that all reception colleagues fully support our Practice Mission Statement to provide professional accessible, quality healthcare services for our patients, and demonstrate the Practice values. Answering telephone calls quickly and efficiently, as per practice guidelines and protocols, and dealing with simple complaints professionally, are key, as well as contributing towards the Practice continuous quality improvement, by demonstrating quality improvements for disease prevalence, and care quality outcomes for patients Key Duties & Responsibilities Answer incoming telephone calls to the Practice Check patients in for appointments Support patients in using our Total triage online consultation system Deal with Ac requests as appropriate Deal with e-mails sent to practice generic e-mail address Open & close surgery, following the appropriate checklists Understand and use EMIS clinical system as per practice guidelines Deal with patient queries including simple complaints Use appointments system efficiently and effectively Book clinics Deal with TASKS on EMIS LRU referrals Chaperone patients Complete NHS paperwork as required Take responsibility to ensure all deliveries and remittances , including arranging appropriate storage, are dealt with care and due attention, including but not limited to bloods/samples/medicines/stationery/post Dealing with payments for non-NHS services Any other task, as required by the Partnership or Practice Managers Skills & Qualifications: Strong communication skills both verbal written. Adaptable to Change. Organisational skills, basic competency in IT. Able to work at pace with focus on accuracy. GCSE in Maths & English at grade 4-9 or equivalent. NVQ in Customer Service would be beneficial. Confidentiality: -In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately -In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential -Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will support the Practice on the full range of promotion and management of their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include (but will not be limited to): -Maintaining an up-to-date knowledge of health and safety and infection control (statutory and best practice guidelines) and ensure implementation across the business - Using personal security systems within the workplace, according to practice guidelines - Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks across the business - Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills, and initiate and manage the training of others - Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards, and initiating remedial / corrective action where needed - Actively identifying, reporting, and correcting health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised - Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas generally clean, identifying issues and hazards / risks in relation to other work areas within the business, and assuming responsibility in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness across the business in consultation (where appropriate) with other sector managers - Maintenance of team areas and work space standards - Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: - Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development - Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: - Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk - Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision - Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance - Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs - Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: -Communicate effectively with other team members - Communicate effectively with patients and carers - Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post holder will: -Apply practice policies, standards and guidance - Discuss with other team members how policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work - Participate in audit where appropriate Please note: The duties and responsibilities contained within this Job Description are indicative but not exhaustive. The post holder may be required to undertake other work as deemed necessary by the Practice Manager. This Job Description may change in light of future developments.

title: Senior Administrator
description: St Stephens Health Centre is seeking an experienced, proactive and highly organised Senior Administrator to join our friendly and supportive practice team. This is an important senior role within the practice, supporting the management team and providing day-to-day leadership and coordination across our administration and coding teams. The successful candidate will help ensure that administrative workflows linked to patient care are completed safely, efficiently and to a consistently high standard. The role also has a broader operational remit, supporting the Deputy Practice Manager with premises, building works, health and safety compliance and certification requirements, IT systems and service improvement. We are looking for someone who understands the demands of a busy GP practice, can confidently prioritise and delegate work, and is comfortable taking ownership of operational issues. Strong NHS primary care experience and working knowledge of EMIS Web are essential. At St Stephens Health Centre, our values of Respect, Empower and Compassion are at the heart of everything we do. The postholder will also support the Deputy Practice Manager with premises and compliance responsibilities. This includes coordinating contractors and building works, maintaining health and safety documentation, risk assessments, mandatory certificates, COSHH information, asset registers, PAT testing and equipment calibration. The role requires excellent organisation, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise, delegate and respond calmly to changing demands in a busy GP practice. The Senior Administrator plays a key role in supporting the safe and effective day-to-day running of St Stephens Health Centre. Working closely with the Deputy Practice Manager and wider management team, the postholder will lead and coordinate administrative and coding functions while also supporting important operational, premises and compliance responsibilities. This is a varied and fast-paced role requiring excellent organisational skills, sound judgement, leadership capability and previous experience within primary care or an NHS setting. Oversee the day-to-day workflows of the administration and coding teams Coordinate rotas, shift cover and annual leave to maintain safe service delivery Support patient administration processes, including referrals, triaging, registrations, safeguarding workflows, medical records and results handling Coordinate coding and document-management processes, ensuring work is completed accurately and within agreed timescales Support clinical session planning, room allocation and clinician rota arrangements Provide day-to-day guidance and support to administrative staff and contribute to induction, training, recruitment and succession planning Support the Deputy Practice Manager with premises management, planned and reactive building works, contractors and maintenance requirements Help maintain health and safety documentation, risk assessments, mandatory premises certificates, COSHH records, asset registers, PAT testing and equipment calibration Monitor outstanding compliance and maintenance actions and liaise with contractors, suppliers and external services where required Support procurement, local IT and systems issues, CQC readiness and service-improvement work Provide senior operational cover across administration and reception functions when required The successful candidate will be expected to work flexibly from Monday to Friday, manage competing priorities and take ownership of delegated actions. They will need to work collaboratively across clinical and non-clinical teams.
