This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a dedicated team committed to providing high-quality patient care and supporting the local community. The GP Receptionist will be responsible for providing efficient and professional reception and administrative support to patients, doctors and other members of the practice team. Key responsibilities include: Answering incoming telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries in a polite and professional manner. Booking, cancelling and rearranging patient appointments. Managing patient requests and assisting with the daily triage list in accordance with practice procedures. Supporting GPs and other healthcare professionals with their day-to-day administrative duties. Greeting patients and assisting them at the reception desk. Processing patient registrations and updating patient records accurately. Handling prescription requests and directing queries to the appropriate team. Managing incoming correspondence, emails and administrative tasks. Maintaining patient confidentiality and following GDPR and practice policies. Working closely with colleagues to ensure the smooth and efficient running of the practice. The successful candidate must be able to prioritise their workload, remain calm under pressure and provide excellent patient service at all times. To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception and administrative duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, patient registration, booking appointments, processing of information (electronic and hard copy) and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers.

title: Receptionist - GP Surgery
description: This is not for locum agencies For queries, please email i.sanghera@nhs.net Southall Medical Centre has an exciting new vacancy for a part-time (20-25 hours/week) receptionist / administrator to join our dynamic admin team! No prior GP practice experience is required, however the ideal candidate must be familiar with the role of primary care / GPs in the NHS. Good IT and computer skills are essential for this position. Key responsibilities and duties include: Triaging appointment requests and booking appointments appropriately for patients Handling incoming telephone calls to the surgery Processing repeat prescriptions according to practice policy Scanning and processing medical documents through SystmOne (clinical system) Completing tasks set by the practice manager and the doctors / clinicians Opening and closing front doors in line with opening times Greeting patients kindly and courteously Working as part of a team collaboratively with other team members Preparing the surgery, waiting area, consulting rooms in preparation for clinics You must be a friendly, courteous people-person as this role primarily involves handling patient queries and have a strong work-ethic and resolve to help provide excellent patient care, in line with our practice vision. Ability to speak Panjabi, Hindi, Gujarati or Urdu would also be extremely beneficial for this position. The role of reception / administrator is mainly an administrative role, and requires excellent people-person and communication skills, due to the patient-facing nature of the role. Duties and responsibilities of receptionists include, but are not limited to: appointments, handling telephone calls, document workflows, processing repeat prescription requests, completing tasks set by practice manager or doctors, opening/closing front doors, maintaining cleanliness of waiting area and consulting rooms, keeping noticeboards and patient areas up-to-date, working collaboratively as part of our practice team. The ideal candidate will have some experience of the NHS, however no previous GP surgery employment is required. Strong work-ethic, commitment to the role, flexibility and efficiency are key traits in a successful applicant. Although you will be well-supported by our existing administrative and management team, you must be able to work independently, autonomously, with a problem-solving and can-do attitude. As the first port of call for our patients, a friendly and warm welcome and excellent communication skills are crucial to this role. The surgery is fully computerised, so good IT and computer skills are a necessity. Successful applicants will be proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) as well as SystmOne (clinical system training provided).

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are looking for a bright, friendly, self motivated, responsible and reliable individual to join the reception team in this busy GP Surgery. The role is part-time at 25 hours per week delivered in 5 hour shifts across the week, but we require flexibility to schedule for morning or afternoon shifts and cover others whilst on leave. 1. To provide positive, friendly and helpful customer service to our patients, both in person and on the telephone. 2. Book, confirm and cancel appointments and handle enquiries 3. Compose, print, mail and scan correspondence 4. Ensure the correct processing of administrative tasks 5. Protects patients' rights by maintaining confidentiality of personal and financial information. 6. Maintain business office inventory and equipment by checking stock to determine inventory level; anticipating needed supplies; placing and expediting orders for supplies; verifying receipt of supplies; scheduling equipment service and repairs 7. Maintain operations by following policies and procedures; reporting needed changes. 8. Support and promote Health and Safety practice at the surgery 9. Support and cover other staff members as necessary Key Qualities: Excellent telephone and inter-personal manner, Customer Facing Skills, Multi-tasking, Maintaining Inventory, Ability to work independently and within a team, Flexibility, Excellent Time Management and Organisational skills, the ability to demonstrate initiative and responsibility. Attention to detail, Professionalism, Quality Focus, Able to take personal responsibility and deliver a high quality standard of work. Main Duties:

title: Senior Administrator
description: We are seeking a highly organised, proactive and experienced Senior Administrator to join our busy, friendly and supportive team at Speedwell Practice. The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of administrative services across the practice. They will lead and support the administration team while delivering efficient, patient-focused services that contribute to high standards of care, regulatory compliance and practice performance. We are looking for someone who is enthusiastic, motivated, a strong team player and willing to contribute positively to our welcoming practice environment. The role involves overseeing patient registration processes, clinical recall programmes, document management, workflow allocation, referral processing, prescription support and the maintenance of accurate patient records using EMIS Web and Docman. The post holder will also support the achievement of Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) targets and other contractual requirements through effective patient recall and engagement processes. As a Senior Administrator, you will act as a point of escalation for administrative queries, contribute to service improvement initiatives, support staff development and work collaboratively with clinicians, management and external agencies to ensure safe, efficient and high-quality patient care. Job Responsibilities The post holder will strive to maintain quality and efficiency within the practice and will: Provide day-to-day supervision, guidance and support to the administration team. Oversee patient registration and registration workflow processes. Manage document scanning, coding and workflow allocation using EMIS Web and Docman. Coordinate and monitor patient recall programmes, including: QOF recalls Cytology recalls Immunisation recalls NHS Health Check recalls Learning Disability recalls Diabetes recalls Other long-term condition recalls Support the management of appointment scheduling and patient communications. Process referrals, prescription requests and other clinical administration tasks. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records in accordance with information governance requirements. Liaise with external organisations regarding the archiving and retrieval of patient medical records. Monitor administrative performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and patient experience. Support the Practice Manager, Deputy Practice Manager and GP partners in achieving operational and service delivery objectives. Assist with staff training, induction and the development of administrative procedures. Support the practice in achieving QOF targets and other contractual requirements. Promote a culture of quality improvement, teamwork and patient-centred care. Alert relevant team members to issues relating to quality, safety and risk. Assess own performance and take responsibility for actions, either independently or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on individual and team activities and suggesting improvements. Work effectively with individuals and external agencies to meet patients' needs. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Participate in practice meetings and administrative team meetings as required. Participate in audits and quality improvement activities where appropriate.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: The Law Medical Group Practice is seeking a reliable and organised Receptionist to join the team at its Wembley branch. The practice is committed to delivering high quality primary care services to its local community and ensuring smooth day to day patient flow through efficient administrative and reception support. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the clinical and non clinical teams by undertaking a range of front of house and administrative duties. This will include managing appointments through EMIS, handling patient queries, processing incoming correspondence and ensuring information is accurately directed to the relevant clinicians in a timely manner. The role will involve full front of house responsibilities, including welcoming and directing patients, responding to queries and providing a professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. Working Pattern: Part Time, 27.5 Hours per Week The working hours are Monday to Friday, 1:00 pm to 6:30 pm. Please note: The working days and hours are non negotiable . Applicants must be able to commit to this working pattern. Eligibility: Applicants must be UK citizens and have a minimum of five years of work experience in the UK. The role involves providing comprehensive reception support to the multidisciplinary team within the practice. Key responsibilities include managing patient interactions, handling incoming correspondence, and ensuring accurate distribution of information to clinicians. The position includes front-desk duties such as greeting and directing patients, managing the appointment system using EMIS , booking appointments, responding to patient enquiries, and supporting the smooth and efficient day-to-day operation of the practice. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator/Receptionist . There may occasionally be a requirement to carry out other duties depending on workload, operational needs, and staffing levels. Primary Responsibilities Receive and process correspondence from hospitals, external healthcare providers, and other agencies. Scan and upload documents onto the EMIS clinical system, ensuring accurate patient record management. Review and appropriately allocate documents within EMIS , forwarding them to the relevant clinician for review and action. Initiate and respond to requests from patients, practice staff, and external healthcare agencies in a professional and timely manner. Photocopy and prepare documentation as required by clinicians and practice staff. Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence to ensure continuity of service. Accurately input patient information and updates into EMIS where required. Manage and resolve patient queries efficiently, escalating issues where appropriate. Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient reception environment at all times. Support the clinical team with day-to-day operational tasks as required. Complete tasks relating to patient results, correspondence, and clinical letters where appropriate. Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in managing changing workloads and priorities to ensure the smooth operation of the practice. Use EMIS and other digital systems effectively for patient record management, appointment scheduling, and internal communication. Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Medical Receptionist may also be required to: Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system using EMIS . Process appointment requests received in person, by telephone, and via online systems. Answer incoming telephone calls and direct them appropriately or deal with enquiries where possible. Signpost patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or NHS service. Support practice audits and administrative reviews as directed by management. Process incoming electronic communications and documents where required. Scan and attach patient-related documentation accurately to patient records within EMIS . Carry out opening and closing procedures in accordance with the practice rota and operational requirements.

title: GP Receptionist / Administrator
description: A GP practice receptionist/administrator's job involves a mix of front-facing patient support and back-office administrative tasks, including greeting patients, answering phones, scheduling appointments, processing registrations, managing correspondence, handling prescriptions, and data entry into the practice's computer system. They are crucial for the smooth operation of the practice, requiring strong communication, organization, and IT skills. Patient and Visitor Interaction Receive and direct patients, visitors, and staff in person or over the phone. Provide general assistance and answer general enquiries about services and results. Assist patients in accessing the most appropriate healthcare professional. Appointments and scheduling Book new and follow-up appointments. Manage the appointment system and deal with the reception area. Administration and data management Process new patient registrations and handle patient records. File, retrieve, scan, and manage patient-related documents and correspondence. Enter data into computer systems. Process and prepare repeat prescriptions. Communication and support Answer and route incoming telephone calls and take messages. Handle incoming and outgoing correspondence and mail. Provide secretarial and administrative support to the doctors, nurses, and practice manager. Action task requests from clinical staff and external health organisations. To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception and administrative duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, patient registration, booking appointments, processing of information (electronic and hard copy) and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, patient deductions, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Undertake general reception and administrative duties. To receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice Organise appointments on the computerised appointments system, maintaining an awareness of the partners rota and prevailing conditions that could affect the optimum management of appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Take accurate messages, assessing their urgency, and passing on the information appropriately to doctors, nurses and other staff attached to the practice Use tact, diplomacy and care when dealing with patients who may be upset, including those who may react aggressively or abusively To undertake a variety of administrative tasks adhering to set practice protocols and to implement and initiate new policies where necessary Cover where necessary in the absence of other receptionists/administrators on sick or annual leave etc. Undertake general administrative duties. To undertake any other duties which may reasonably be delegated by the Partners and the Practice Manager Make appointments and check in patients on the computerised appointments system, maintaining an awareness of the partners rota and prevailing conditions that could affect the optimum management of appointments. Advise new patients of the registration process. Register patients appropriately, including the forwarding/receipt of patients records and amendment and updating of patient details and direct to appropriate waiting area Prepare repeat prescriptions and record them on the computer following practice protocols, being aware of the restrictions applied to the controlled drugs issuing and collection procedures File and archive records, letters and reports Arrange appointments and transport for patients, including emergency transport arrangements Sort incoming and outgoing mail, emails and faxes as necessary Ensure timely and appropriate transportation or postage of samples/ specimens to hospital Provide IT support and troubleshooting for the practice. Receive payments from patients and record accurately in cash receipt books and provide receipts Be aware of external organisations and their relationship with the practice e.g. Barnet Federation Hub and choose and book system Keep the reception office, records and waiting rooms tidy and undertake any other tasks which contribute to the smooth and efficient organisation of these areas Attend suitable training sessions or courses, approved by the Practice Manager, in order to enhance skills and knowledge including online training through Blue Stream Academy.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Abbey Medical Centre Camden, London NW8 OAG. We are seeking committed receptionists, who demonstrate enthusiasm for working in primary care, with a genuine interest in working with patients and contributing to the delivery of high quality health care. Applicants should be courteous, highly motivated, pro-active and good team players, able to project a positive and friendly image to patients/visitors. These posts are full time/part time . Each of the posts available may be suitable for job share. Part Time will also be considered (over 5 days). This will involve working on reception (front desk), back office function including processing repeat prescriptions, scanning, summarising, filing medical records.etc. The job will be varied and time will be split between the roles. The surgery uses EMISWeb/DOCMAN 10 as their clinical system. The following are the core responsibilities of the receptionist/administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: a. Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system b. Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments c. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately d. Action all incoming faxes e. Signpost patients to the correct service f. Process incoming and outgoing mail g. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies h. Process referrals to external agencies such as secondary care using the electronic referral system (ERS) i. Process calling letters are requested j. Process all DNA letters in accordance with current policy k. Action GP2GP tasks l. Read code data on EMIS Web m. Photocopy documentation as required n. File and store records as required o. Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as required p. Input data into the patients healthcare records as necessary q. Scanning of patient related documentation and attaching scanned documents to patients healthcare records r. Process requests for information i.e. SAR, insurance / solicitors letters and DVLA forms to the administrative team s. Manage all queries (including administrative queries) as necessary in an efficient manner t. Carry out system searches as requested u. Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times v. Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards w. Support all clinical staff with general tasks as requested Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the medical administrator may be requested to: a. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead b. Produce meeting agendas and record the minutes of meetings c. Support administrative and reception staff, providing cover during staff absences d. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota e. As required support in the management of repeat prescriptions, ensuring they are processed accurately and efficiently f. Ordering and monitoring of stationery supplies
